subject: Tranche orchestration: APAC-first capacity ask for Q3-Q4 ramp
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Tranche orchestration: APAC-first capacity ask for Q3-Q4 ramp

Team —

Quick background: OrionAI (who we've been piloting with) just signaled a much larger multi-region expansion that prefers an APAC-first go-live in Singapore by late Aug (their marketing event is 9/15). They are asking for committed dedicated capacity for inference (L2 text gen workloads) plus burst capacity for evaluation days.

High-level asks from their procurement:
- Q3 (Aug–Sep): sustained 16 vGPU-equivalents (H100 smallish instances) in SG region, with ability to burst to 40 for 48-hour eval windows twice in Sept.
- Q4 (Oct–Dec): scale to 40 sustained with 2x monthly burst windows.

They want a tranche-based contract: initial small commit (trial/pricing credit) followed by escalation steps tied to product milestones. They also asked for networking details (peering, egress limits) and a fallback plan to our hosted US region in case SG provisioning misses the event.

Action items I need internal help on:
- Priyom: a realistic mapping of 16 sustained / 40 burst to our dedicated pool units (how many GPUs, expected throughput, and throughput headroom). Include quantization and batching profiles that reduce peak GPU counts.
- Laura: pricing sketch for tranche1 (trial) and tranche2 (ramp) incl. amortized infra delta and suggested SLA credit if we miss burst windows.
- Hannah: feasibility note on Singapore new region onboarding (KMS, VPC peering timeline, SOC2 evidence). Can we commit to provisioning by 8/20 if we prioritize?
- Marissa: if we need to re-orchestrate regional pool priorities, what's the expected impact on other Q3 deals?

Attaching a draft tranche schedule and network diagram (tranche_plan_v3.xlsx / apac_network_diagram.pdf).

David

--
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tranche orchestration: APAC-first capacity ask for Q3-Q4 ramp

David / team —

I've run the initial numbers against our capacity model. Short summary:
- 16 sustained vGPU-equivalents (target H100 perf) maps to roughly 4 physical H100-80GB GPUs if we run aggressive quantization and continuous batching. Without quantization it's closer to 8 physical GPUs.
- 40 burst for 48 hours needs an ephemeral pool of ~10–12 H100s to keep latency under 200ms for OrionAI's 1.2k TPS load profile during eval windows.

Tradeoffs and levers:
- Quantization to 4-bit + mixed precision inference reduces physical GPU needs by ~2x on gen workloads but requires ML validation (we should scope an eval).
- Prefix KV caching for repeated prompts during demos will reduce token compute by up to 35% during the 48-hour bursts, allowing lower burst pool sizes in practice.
- If we use smaller instances (A100 80GB) we need 6–8 physical to hit sustained targets but burst headroom goes up since those are cheaper/denser for short windows.

I recommend the following tranche mapping:
- Tranche 0 (pilot, July–Aug): Reserve 2 H100s dedicated (sustained) + ability to allocate 4 additional H100s for two 48-hour bursts (ephemeral). Purpose: validation and ML quantization tests.
- Tranche 1 (post-event Sept–Oct): Move to 6 H100s sustained + ability to burst to 12. Includes automated batching rules and KV prefix caching.
- Tranche 2 (Nov onward): 12–14 H100s sustained (targeting 40 vGPU-equivalents via quantization and instance mix) with structured burst policy.

I'll attach a worksheet with the mapping (tranche_plan_v3.xlsx) and estimated cost model by GPU type. This is feasible but requires clear prioritization on the provisioning timeline (see Hannah).

- Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tranche orchestration: APAC-first capacity ask for Q3-Q4 ramp

David / all —

Feasibility note on Singapore onboarding: we can push SG provisioning to target 8/20 but it will need the following gating items completed by 7/15:
- KMS access approvals and HSM key creation (security team window: 7/6–7/12)
- VPC peering and egress policy finalized with OrionAI networking (they've agreed to provide CIDR ranges by 6/10)
- Physical instance availability confirmation from supply (operations needs to confirm H100 availability in our SG partner pool by 6/10)

Risk: if H100 inventory isn't available we can do a hybrid approach (A100 sustained + H100 ephemeral bursts) but that increases networking churn and slightly raises per-token cost (~12–18%). Other risk is audit readiness (SOC2 addition for region) — security is OK with an accelerated scope but it will add ~2 weeks of documentation work.

If we prioritize, I suggest committing to Tranche 0 (pilot) with the hybrid instance approach (2 A100 sustained + access to 6 ephemeral H100 for the Sept burst). This buys us time to secure H100 capacity and validate quantization.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tranche orchestration: APAC-first capacity ask for Q3-Q4 ramp

Team —

Pricing sketch attached (commit_terms_summary.docx). Key points:
- Tranche 0 (pilot): 30% discount on unit rates for first 8 weeks + 100% credit for 2x 48-hour burst windows as good-faith (limited to 6 H100s).
- Tranche 1: ramp pricing assumes 6 H100 sustained; we're proposing a blended committed rate that reduces after 3 months to reflect steady-state utilization.
- SLA credit: for missed burst availability we propose a one-time service credit equal to 5% of monthly committed spend for the tranche period (capped). This is stricter than usual but helpful for closing.

Impact on revenue/ops: committing to a hybrid H100/A100 approach reduces our margin on tranche 0 (pilot) by ~9% but preserves a higher probability of conversion. Legal will want to see the exact wording on burst guarantees (we should avoid explicit penalties that create open-ended exposure).

Next step: David, if you want to present this to Orion next week I can turn the sketch into a formal SOW template.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett

David / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed tranche roadmap. From Orion's side:
- The event on 9/15 is fixed and we'd like to lock the pilot tranche (Tranche 0) now if we can get a written confirmation on the burst windows and the ability to scale to 40 vGPU-equivalents by Nov.
- On quantization: our ML team is happy to run validation with Redwood on a small sample workload in July — we'd need the access plan and data retention terms documented.
- On networking: Neura (Sofia) will coordinate the VPC ranges and provide peering contact. We expect egress budget of ~8TB/month to start; please confirm if that fits the SG estimate.

Can we schedule a 30-min call next week (Mon or Wed preferred) to finalize SOW bullet points and calendarize provisioning milestones?

Sunil
Head of Platform Partnerships, OrionAI
